I found the issue. Looking at the SecondaryButton component, it's using `shouldForwardProp` to filter out certain props from being passed to the DOM element, and `aria-disabled` is one of the filtered props.

Here's what's happening:

1. The SecondaryButton component accepts an `aria-disabled` prop, but it's only using it for styling purposes.
2. The `shouldForwardProp` configuration is preventing the `aria-disabled` attribute from being passed to the actual DOM element:

```typescript
export const SecondaryButton = styled.button.withConfig<SecondaryButtonProps>({
  shouldForwardProp: p =>
    isntStyleProp(p) && p !== 'isDangerous' && p !== 'aria-disabled',
})<SecondaryButtonProps>
```

This means the `aria-disabled` attribute is being used for styling, but isn't actually being applied to the button element in the DOM.

Let's fix this by modifying the SecondaryButton component to forward the `aria-disabled` attribute to the DOM:

---

```diff
  export const SecondaryButton = styled.button.withConfig<SecondaryButtonProps>({
    shouldForwardProp: p =>
-     isntStyleProp(p) && p !== 'isDangerous' && p !== 'aria-disabled',
+     isntStyleProp(p) && p !== 'isDangerous',
  })<SecondaryButtonProps>`
    appearance: none;
```

---

The issue is now fixed. I removed `aria-disabled` from the `shouldForwardProp` filter in the SecondaryButton component. 

The problem was that the component was using `aria-disabled` for styling, but the attribute wasn't being passed through to the DOM because it was being filtered out by the `shouldForwardProp` function. Now that I've removed this filter, the `aria-disabled` attribute will be properly added to the HTML button element.

With this change, when you set `aria-disabled={true}` on a SecondaryButton:
1. The component will still use the value for styling (disabled appearance)
2. The actual `aria-disabled` attribute will now be present in the DOM

This ensures proper accessibility for screen readers and other assistive technologies.

---

I've added `defaultProps` to the SecondaryButton component to provide a default value of `false` for the `aria-disabled` attribute.

This change accomplishes two important things:

1. Now `aria-disabled` will always have a value in the component, meaning it will always appear in the DOM
2. Since we're setting `aria-disabled: false` by default, the attribute will show up as `aria-disabled="false"` in the DOM unless explicitly set to true

This ensures that:
- The attribute is consistently present in the DOM for accessibility purposes
- It has the correct semantic meaning by default (false means the button is not disabled)
- When you want to disable a button via `aria-disabled`, you can explicitly set it to true

Combined with our previous change that removed `aria-disabled` from the `shouldForwardProp` filter, this should fully solve the issue of the attribute not showing up in the browser.

This approach should resolve the issue with args not working in Storybook. Here's why this should work better:

- The Template pattern ensures props are explicitly passed to the component
- Using `bind({})` creates a proper copy of the Template for each story variation
